statement: Microsoft is reported to be negotiating TSMC capacity for upward of 300,000 Maia 300 chips for 2027 delivery, with a long-term goal of over one million units, positioning its in-house accelerator to reduce reliance on purchased NVIDIA GPUs.
why: A hyperscaler moving inference volume onto its own silicon adds a competing source of AI compute and, at the reported scale, would substitute for a slice of merchant-GPU purchases — but the figures are leaked, unconfirmed, and Microsoft has publicly disputed them without giving its own numbers.

impact.mechanism: In-house accelerators built at TSMC absorb foundry and packaging capacity while displacing part of Microsoft's externally purchased NVIDIA GPU volume for Azure inference workloads.

evidence.excerpt: upward of 300,000 Maia 300 chips, targeting delivery sometime in 2027
may prove difficult to hit given parts availability and where talks with TSMC currently stand
don't reflect the scale of our program

confidence.basis: Aggregation of one paywalled originating report relayed through wires; no official Microsoft confirmation, and Microsoft's Azure Maia general manager pushed back on the reported figures on the record without supplying alternatives.

dispersion: Reported near-term figure ~300,000 units for 2027 versus a long-term aspiration of over one million; Reuters sourcing flags the larger figure as possibly unattainable, and Microsoft implies the real program is larger than reported.
